subject: Pay slope calibration: local-market scaling & offer guidance
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Local pay-slope proposal: request for review

Team,

Putting this draft out for quick review before we ask People Ops for a formal headcount/comp approval. High level:
- Goal: tighten offer slope for L3-L6 across US metros to reduce variance while preserving competitiveness in high-cost cities.
- Proposal attached: comp-band-proposal-v1.xlsx (tabs: slope-method, geo-multipliers, sample-offers).

Key asks:
1) Is the proposed slope cap (-10% / +15% around anchor) acceptable for hiring managers?
2) Do the geo multipliers reflect what teams are seeing in SF/NY/SEA/BOS?
3) Any regulatory or payroll concerns we should flag to Finance?

I recommend we run a 6-week pilot for new offers and surface metrics (accept rate, time-to-offer, cost delta). Planning notes + Drive link below.

Drive (drafts): https://drive.company.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pay-slope-drafts

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Talent Partner, Hiring Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: comp-band-proposal-v1.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Local pay-slope proposal: request for review

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
>
> Putting this draft out for quick review before we ask People Ops for a formal headcount/comp approval.

Thanks Aisha — good start. A few quick notes after a skim and a call with Sierra Compensation this morning:
- Benchmarks: their Q3 feed shows wider upper-tail variance in SF for L5-L6 (about +18% vs our anchor) — I attached their summary.
- Suggest we: (a) keep anchor intact, (b) allow a metro-adjust modifier +1.12 for SF/SV, +1.08 for NYC, +1.06 for SEA.
- For offer slope, prefer a percentile-based cap (50th -> 75th) rather than hard +/- %. Easier to communicate to hiring managers.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync with Sierra and Ben Morales from PeopleMetrics for Thurs to walk through the raw data.

Karthik
Director, Compensation & Analytics

Attachment: sierra-benchmarks-q3-2026.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Local pay-slope proposal: request for review

Thanks both — quick reactions and operational asks:
- Ops impact: we need a clear table for recruiters with the final multiplier per city and the fallback rules when a hiring manager requests above-band offers.
- Candidate-facing framing: short script and email template we can use to explain market adjustments.
- Pilot cohort: recommend Eng (backend) and Solutions (mid-market AE) for the pilot — both are high volume and will stress offer cadence.

Action items:
- Karthik: can you convert the slope into an "accept-range" (50th-75th) and share a one-pager?
- Aisha: can you produce the candidate communication templates and the pilot cohort list?
- Michael: can you confirm whether Payroll needs a separate code for geo multipliers?

Marissa
Head of Talent Programs

> On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 11:03 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Thanks Aisha — good start. A few quick notes after a skim and a call with Sierra Compensation this morning...

From: Sierra Compensation <sierra@compbench.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Local pay-slope proposal: request for review — Q3 summary attached

Hi Aisha / Karthik / Marissa,

Pleasure speaking yesterday. Attached is the Q3 summary we discussed (sierra-benchmarks-q3-2026.pdf). Highlights:
- SF and NYC show the largest upward skew for senior engineering roles; median-to-75th spread is ~12-18% depending on specialism.
- Mid-market cities (Austin, Denver) show modest uplifts (~+4-8%).
- Our recommended approach: anchor at market median, expose metro multipliers, and cap top-of-band offers to the 90th percentile for exec-level roles only.

If useful, Ben Morales from PeopleMetrics can run a cohort-level simulation against your offer history to estimate cost and accept-rate impact.

Best,
Sierra
Sierra Compensation
Sierra@compbench.com

Attachment: sierra-benchmarks-q3-2026.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pay slope calibration: local-market scaling & offer guidance

Thanks team — I reviewed the attachments and Sierra's summary. Approve proceeding to a time-boxed pilot as you recommended. Please proceed with the following steps by end of next week: 
1) Aisha: finalize the candidate communication templates and pilot list; share to Drive.
2) Karthik: publish the one-pager with the accept-range table and metro multipliers; include a short FAQ for managers.
3) Michael: confirm payroll code and cost center tagging for geo multipliers; include Finance in the rollout email.

I want a short exec summary for the October SLT packet (1 page — impact on offers and estimated incremental run-rate). If the pilot results look good, we'll propose a permanent update in Q1.

Laura Bennett
VP, People & Talent
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot-rollout-checklist.docx
